q: The differential entropy h(X) = −∫ f(x) log f(x) dx for a continuous random variable differs from discrete entropy in that:
opts: It is invariant under invertible transformations
It can be negative and is not invariant under non-linear reparametrization (but changes by log|J| under linear maps)
It equals H(X) when X is quantized
exp: Differential entropy can be negative (e.g., Uniform[0, ε] for small ε). Under y = ax, h(Y) = h(X) + log|a|. It lacks the operational meaning of discrete entropy without conditioning on a resolution.
